Antarctic Desert.text: In Antarctica, meteorites keep so well that ones over a million years old turn up, a few of them from the Moon and Mars.
Antarctic Desert.evidence: Antarctica provides a unique environment for the study of meteorites: the dry polar desert preserves them well, and meteorites older than a million years have been found. ... Most meteorites come from asteroids, but a few meteorites found in Antarctica came from the Moon and Mars.

Arctic Desert.text: It spans Canada, Alaska, Greenland, the Nordic countries and Russia; "Arctic" comes from the Greek for "near the Bear".
Arctic Desert.where: Canada, Finland, Greenland, Iceland, Norway, Russia, Sweden, United States (Alaska)
Arctic Desert.evidence: The word Arctic comes from the Greek word ἀρκτικός arktikos "near the Bear, northern" and from the word ἄρκτος arktos meaning "bear," named for either the constellation known as Ursa Major, the "Great Bear"

Sahara Desert.text: Spanning 12 countries, from Morocco to Egypt, it is so large and bright it could in theory be detected from other stars.
Sahara Desert.where: Algeria, Chad, Egypt, Eritrea, Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, Sudan, Tunisia, Western Sahara
Sahara Desert.evidence: The Sahara is so large and bright that, in theory, it could be detected from other stars as a surface feature of Earth, with near-current technology.

Arabian Desert.text: Spanning Saudi Arabia and ten other countries, it holds the Empty Quarter, the world's largest continuous body of sand.
Arabian Desert.where: Egypt (Sinai Peninsula), Iraq, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Yemen
Arabian Desert.evidence: At its southern end is Ar-Rub' al-Khali (The Empty Quarter), the largest continuous body of sand in the world.

Great Australian Desert.text: In Australia, it has the largest population of feral camels in the world.
Great Australian Desert.evidence: The Australian desert has the largest population of feral camels in the world.

Gobi Desert.text: In China and Mongolia, its temperatures can change by as much as 35 °C within 24 hours.
Gobi Desert.evidence: However, the climate of the Gobi is one of great extremes, with rapid changes of temperature of as much as 35 °C (63 °F) in 24-hour spans.

Kalahari Desert.text: In Botswana, Namibia and South Africa, its name comes from Tswana words meaning "the great thirst" or "a waterless place".
Kalahari Desert.evidence: Kalahari is derived from the Tswana word Kgala, meaning "the great thirst", or Kgalagadi, meaning "a waterless place";

Patagonian Desert.text: In Argentina and Chile, it formed in the rain shadow of the Andes, which block moisture from the Pacific.
Patagonian Desert.evidence: The Andes, to the desert's west, are the primary reason for the Patagonian desert status as they inhibit the westerly flow of moisture from the southern Pacific from reaching inland. This creates a rain shadow that accounts for the formation of the desert

Syrian Desert.text: Spanning Syria, Jordan, Iraq and Saudi Arabia, it is where the golden hamster comes from.
Syrian Desert.evidence: The Syrian Desert is the origin of the golden hamster.

Great Basin Desert.text: In Nevada, Utah, California and Idaho, it has more than 33 peaks above 9,800 feet (3,000 m).
Great Basin Desert.evidence: There are more than 33 peaks within the desert with summits higher than 9,800 feet (3,000 m),
